label: Mirror fork for necessitarians; contrast gap of invariant sources (inference)
rule: Collapse with essence-grounded possibility identifies every unexcluded world with the actual one; case analysis on which premise of the mirror argument fails
meaning: Clause 1 restates collapse with essence-grounded possibility (one term from the two; it records no further cost). Clauses 2-4 locate the necessitarian's exit: with reversal and the possibility principle, some essential truth separates w from σ w (a nature containing orientation, option 1); with preservation but without the possibility principle, σ w is unexcluded and impossible (brute, option 3); with the possibility principle and preservation, σ w = w and no feature is reversed (no distinct mirror image, option 2). Clause 5: a necessitating rule that singles out w is itself not mirror-invariant at w. Clause 6 is the relation-of-reason certificate's clause 1 with a general explanandum: for every source whose real determinations are invariant over accessible worlds no intrinsic fact discriminates this handedness from the other. Clause 7: an orientation token (a real determination) with an equally pure alternative is excluded at an actual root by the requirement-form purity premises (the handedness instance of lane P's mechanism, proved from the declarations on main); parity in purity is assumed. Clause 9: under essence grounding necessity, possibility and factivity, preservation is the mirror image's accessibility. Clause 10: option 1 at a root (an orientation in the root's ESSENCE_5 nature) is excluded only through the open carriage bridge from ESSENCE_5 truths to orientation tokens; without it clause 7 says nothing about a root's nature. With σ the plain reflection P, option 1 is available at creaturely natures on dispositional essentialism (the weak interaction is not reflection-invariant); with σ read as CPT conjugation it is not. The certificate does not favour personal over impersonal accounts; it presses necessitarian accounts of either kind and any claim that an invariant source's intrinsic profile explains the contrast.
